title: Greywater Bay Rising Anew
premise: True-crime podcaster Sebastian Sandoval has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidents, all connected to Greywater Bay's founding families. When she obtains the diary of Marina Voss, missing for nineteen years, she finds entries written after the date Marina vanished—proof someone kept her captive, and proof the ledger of bribes Marina recorded is still being used to buy silence today. Following the coded ledger through land deeds, church donations, and shell companies, Sebastian closes in on Aldous Crane, the beloved civic patriarch who has been Greywater Bay's secret keeper and executioner for decades. In the flooded tunnels beneath the old cannery, Sebastian finds Marina alive but broken, chooses love for her endangered partner over the safe anonymity she'd built, and exposes Crane publicly—at the cost of burning down the life she once hid inside.
about_author: Isandro Dunmore is the pen name of a former coastal-town journalist who spent a decade covering unsolved disappearances before turning to fiction. He writes from a houseboat on the Pacific Northwest, where the fog never quite lifts.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She records the finale of her podcast season on three 'accidental' deaths, all tied to Greywater Bay's founding families, while hiding her identity behind voice modulation. The emotional beat: quiet triumph shadowed by loneliness—she's solved what police couldn't, and no one can know it was her.

chapters.title: A Package with No Return Address
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. An anonymous envelope arrives containing Marina Voss's diary, missing since 2006. The final entry is dated eleven days after her disappearance. Sebastian's hands shake as she realizes someone wrote those words—and Marina may have been alive long after the bay stopped looking. Beat: dread igniting obsession.

chapters.title: Nineteen Years of Tide Charts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashbacks to Marina's diary entries interleaved. Sebastian reconstructs Marina's last known week: a bookkeeper at Crane Fisheries who noticed numbers that didn't add up. Beat: growing intimacy with a woman she'll never meet, and the first hint the diary is also a code.

chapters.title: The Man Who Built the Boardwalk
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She attends a gala honoring Aldous Crane, Greywater Bay's philanthropic patriarch, and watches him work a crowd like a conductor. He compliments her podcast—by its private working title. Beat: the hunter realizing she has become the hunted.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Marina's diary POV chapters begin alternating in. Her entries reveal a hidden ledger: payments routed through the church restoration fund, the harbor authority, a judge's 'consulting fees.' Beat: Marina's fear curdling into resolve as she decides to copy everything.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She maps her three solved deaths against the ledger's dates and names—each victim received money within a month of dying. Someone cleaned up around Crane's transactions for decades. Beat: cold clarity; this isn't one murder, it's an institution.

chapters.title: Delia
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Delia Reyes, a marine researcher and Sebastian's secret partner of two years, pushes her to go to the FBI. Sebastian refuses—invisibility has kept them both alive. Their fight cracks open the cost of Sebastian's double life. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She discovers the diary's marginal doodles are a numeric cipher keyed to tide tables, unlocking ledger coordinates: properties, dates, amounts. The last decoded line points to the flooded cannery tunnels. Beat: exhilaration tipping into terror—the diary was meant to be found.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Marina's POV. The post-disappearance entries grow fragmented: a basement, a kind captor's guilt, rationed light. Marina keeps writing to stay sane, hiding pages in a wall cavity. Beat: claustrophobic endurance; survival as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Didn't Drown
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She tracks the only officer who questioned the accident rulings in 2006—retired deputy Frank Okafor, now a lighthouse caretaker. He confirms he was warned off, and that the diary's anonymous sender might be his old informant. Beat: an ally gained, hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Crane's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Crane invites her to his estate, offers to fund her podcast 'properly,' and mentions Delia by name. The threat is velvet-soft. Sebastian accepts the check to buy time, hating herself. Beat: corruption's seduction—and the price of playing along.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Her apartment is ransacked; the diary is gone—but she'd already photographed every page. Delia, spooked, gives Sebastian an ultimatum: the story or her. Beat: rock bottom; the two things she loves most are now mutually exclusive.

chapters.title: The Wall Cavity
chapters.summary: Marina's POV, final entries. Marina learns her captor is dying and will be replaced by someone less merciful. She hides the diary with Okafor's informant and prepares to escape through the cannery tunnels during a storm surge. Beat: desperate courage.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Flooded Tunnels
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Acting on the cipher, Sebastian enters the cannery tunnels at low tide and finds a room: bedding, tally marks, Marina's handwriting on the walls. Marina didn't die here. Marina didn't leave here. Beat: vertigo—nineteen years of assumptions collapse.

chapters.title: The Kind Captor
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Okafor identifies the informant: Tomas Reyes—Delia's father, Crane's former enforcer, the man whose conscience kept Marina alive. Sebastian must tell Delia what her father did. Beat: devastating convergence of every thread; love tested past breaking.

chapters.title: Where Is Marina Voss?
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. If Marina escaped in 2006, where has she been? Sebastian traces a trail of cash payments and a woman who never ages her ID photos—a recluse two towns over. Beat: breathless pursuit toward the truth everyone stopped seeking.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Stayed Invisible
chapters.summary: Alternating Sebastian and Marina POV. Sebastian finds Marina alive—guarded, scarred, unwilling to testify. Marina's condition: take down Crane without making her a public exhibit. Beat: two survivors of invisibility recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Storm Surge
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. With Marina's testimony recorded, Sebastian tips off a state investigator—but Crane's people intercept the evidence and take Okafor. The storm knocks out communications; Crane controls the town's levers completely. Beat: the trap closing from every side.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Minutes Under the Cannery
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Marina POV. Marina leads Sebastian through the tunnels to recover the original ledger from Crane's private vault below the estate's seawall. They're discovered; a chase through rising water. Beat: terror, trust forged in floodwater, near-drowning.

chapters.title: The Patriarch Unmasked
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the harbor festival, before the whole town, Sebastian plays the recording and projects the ledger. Crane's composure shatters as decades of bought silence turn to witness after witness stepping forward. Beat: cathartic climax—power exposed in the square it built.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Crane is arrested; Okafor is rescued; Tomas turns himself in and names every accomplice. But Sebastian's cover is blown, her podcast persona dead, her safety gone. Delia comes back—not because Sebastian is safe, but because she finally chose them over invisibility. Beat: grief and grace entwined.

chapters.title: Greywater Bay Rising Anew
chapters.summary: Sebastian and Marina POV, alternating. One year later: the town holds its first truth commission; Marina testifies under her own name; Sebastian publishes the case openly, co-authoring with Marina. On the rebuilt boardwalk, Sebastian realizes some lives must be burned down to be lived. Beat: resolution—rising anew, not returning.
